name: Anthracnose
symptoms: Dark brown to black necrotic spots with concentric rings on leaves, blossoms, and young fruits.
treatment: Apply Copper oxychloride (0.3%) or Carbendazim (0.1%) spray. Prune dead twigs before flowering.

name: Bacterial Canker
symptoms: Water-soaked angular dark lesions surrounded by clear chlorotic halos on leaves.
treatment: Spray Streptocycline (200 ppm) combined with Copper Oxychloride (0.3%) at 15-day intervals.

name: Cutting Weevil
symptoms: Fresh young tender leaves neatly excised or cut in a straight line as if clipped by scissors.
treatment: Spray Quinalphos 25 EC (2 ml/L) or Monocrotophos on newly emerging flushes.

name: Die Back
symptoms: Drying and withering of twigs from the top downwards, followed by progressive brown discoloration.
treatment: Prune affected shoots 5-8 cm below infected zone and apply Bordeaux paste on cut surfaces.

name: Gall Midge
symptoms: Wart-like raised galls or blister formations across upper and lower surfaces of leaves.
treatment: Foliar spray with Dimethoate 30 EC (1.5 ml/L) or Imidacloprid (0.3 ml/L) during emergence.

name: Powdery Mildew
symptoms: White superficial powdery fungal growth covering leaves, panicles, and tender developing fruitlets.
treatment: Dust with Wettable Sulphur (0.2%) or spray Dinocap (0.1%) or Hexaconazole (0.1%).

name: Sooty Mould
symptoms: Thick black velvety superficial layer of fungal coating on leaf surface interfering with photosynthesis.
treatment: Spray systemic insecticide to manage honeydew-secreting scales/hoppers, followed by 5% starch solution.

name: Healthy
symptoms: Normal deep-green glossy foliage, intact leaf margins, zero fungal or necrotic lesions.
treatment: Maintain balanced NPK fertilization, scheduled drip irrigation, and routine seasonal scouting.
